- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward by 2–5% in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.2) within 5 days, model often fails to adjust downward; apply downward bias of 1–4% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is weak (0.1–0.3) and price is trending down; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent volatility; smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ prices unless sentiment strongly signals reversal.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.7 → -0.3 → +0.5), model tends to lag; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to align with sentiment momentum.
